chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, who said: Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, there was among the Children of Israel a believing man, and he had a neighbor who was an infidel. The infidel used to be kind to the believer and show him goodwill in the world. When the infidel died, Allah built for him a house of mud in Hellfire, which protected him from its heat and provided him sustenance from elsewhere. He was told: 'This is because of the kindness you showed to your believing neighbor, So-and-son-of-So, and the goodwill you extended to him in the world.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for a disbeliever who treats a believer with kindness?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (a.s.) narrates this account from Shaykh al-Saduq to illustrate the principle of *al-Hasanah bi-hasaniha* (the good deed receives its like), where a disbeliever's consistent social courtesy (*birr*) toward a believer earns him a specific, mitigated reward in the Hereafter. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between general social goodness, which yields temporal or partial spiritual relief, and the comprehensive faith required for full entry into Paradise.
